title: Cross-variant warmup race causing initial-token throughput collapse on long-context streaming
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Summary: In production across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments we observed sudden and sustained TTFT (time-to-first-token) spikes and tokens/sec collapse for long-context streaming requests that exercise function-calling. Impact started 2025-08-09 02:30 UTC after a rollout of a kernel-selection and prefetch heuristic (rollout rtm/runtime-1.26.2). Symptoms: median TTFT for affected endpoints rose from ~120ms to ~820ms and tokens/sec dropped by ~4x; tail (p95/p99) became multi-second. Multiple enterprise customers reported degraded UX and one support escalation (Customer: DataScribe).

Reproduction: 1) Send streaming chat requests with ~6k-18k context including priming tokens and function-calling payloads. 2) Observe that the server triggers a cross-variant prefetch that flushes/serializes the KV->prefix merge path. 3) Multiple concurrent requests for the same model variant cause a lock contention and per-request serialization of warmup/merge, blocking generation start.

Root cause hypothesis: The new kernel-selection heuristic attempts to co-locate requests onto a warmup path and opportunistically prefetch weights/KV across variant groups. Under realistic tenant fanout patterns this created a short-lived critical section in the prefix-merge path that serializes first-token work across requests. The worst impact happens when function-calling adds extra priming frames (structured tool calls), increasing KV merges per request. The heuristic also bypassed the fast-path snapshotting introduced in runtime-1.24, accidentally forcing a global prefetch barrier for a subset of long-context models.

Immediate mitigations already applied: - Rolled back the kernel-selection heuristic in hosted to the previous stable commit (deployed 2025-08-09 03:15 UTC). - Enabled emergency per-tenant prewarm cap (50 prewarm tokens) to reduce cross-tenant prefetch fanout (deployed 2025-08-09 03:40 UTC). - Added temporary routing rule: long-context streaming routed to warm workers with serialized prewarm disabled for 24 hours. - Opened alert 'ENG-998123-TTFT' with a dedicated oncall channel and dashboard (see attachments). These reduced median TTFT to ~220ms but p99 remained elevated.

Planned permanent fixes: 1) Remove global prefetch barrier: rework prefix-merge to use per-request lockless snapshotting; ensure the fast-path snapshot is used for streaming AND function-calling flows (patch in progress). 2) Implement a per-worker async prefetch queue with backpressure and soft-priority for same-tenant requests to avoid cross-tenant stall. 3) Add a microbench harness in CI that simulates long-context streaming + function-calling to guard against regressions. 4) Add new observability: metric 'kv.merge_block_ms' and 'prefetch_fanout' with tenant tags and increase retention on affected dashboards.

Rollout plan: - Merge patch to canary branch and run throughput tests in perf-lab (target: tokens/sec within 10% of baseline). - Canary deploy eu-west-1 (5% traffic) for 2h, validate TTFT/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. - Gradual ramp to 30% then 100% with automated rollback on >15% regression vs baseline. For Dedicated/Private we will produce a patch release (runtime-1.26.3-hotfix) and provide upgrade notes; we will also supply a one-off emergency configuration toggle for customers who cannot upgrade immediately.

Testing and validation: - Synthetic loadgen scenario 'longstream-fncall-6k' added to perf harness. - Unit tests for prefix-merge snapshot semantics. - End-to-end validation using internal staging with mixed tenant fanout.

Customer comms: Draft for Customer DataScribe prepared, offering timeline and temporary workarounds. Support to proactively reach other customers who surfaced similar issues.

Postmortem plan: Full incident write-up post-resolution with timeline, contributing change, detection gaps, and checklist to prevent kernel-selection regressions.
